questions.q: Why can system integration testing (SIT) pass while user acceptance testing (UAT) still uncovers problems?
options: SIT confirms technical correctness; UAT confirms real business users can actually do their jobs, which a technically correct workflow can still fail at
SIT and UAT always test the exact same things, so this cannot happen
UAT is performed before SIT in every implementation
UAT only tests report formatting, nothing else
questions.explain: SIT is largely a technical/process check run by the project team. UAT tests whether the client's own users can actually perform their real workflows - a gap SIT often cannot see.

questions.q: What is a conference room pilot (CRP) and why does it matter?
options: A final sign-off meeting held after go-live
A slide deck presentation of the proposed configuration
A working session where business users react to the actual configured system well before go-live, surfacing gaps earlier and more cheaply
A meeting exclusively for the project's technical architects
questions.explain: A CRP puts a working, configured system in front of real users before go-live, which surfaces usability and requirement gaps far more cheaply than discovering them during UAT or after go-live.

questions.q: What is the recommended approach when a new requirement surfaces after configuration is already locked?
options: Quietly implement it without telling anyone to avoid delay
Refuse to discuss it under any circumstances
Assess the real impact and raise it through change control so the client understands the trade-off
Automatically extend the project timeline by one month without analysis
questions.explain: A late requirement should be assessed for real impact and raised through change control, so the client sees the trade-offs (timeline, retesting, cost) before deciding.

questions.q: How does a functional consultant's role change during hypercare, the period right after go-live?
options: It stays identical to the configuration phase
The consultant has no responsibilities at all during this period
The consultant only works on reports during hypercare
The consultant shifts to rapid triage - determining whether an issue is a configuration gap, a training gap, or a genuine defect, and resolving or escalating quickly
questions.explain: Hypercare is when real volume and real users meet the system for the first time. The consultant's job becomes fast triage and resolution, since trust in the new system is most fragile in this window.

questions.q: Why does this lesson avoid naming one single branded methodology for the implementation phases?
options: Because Oracle implementations never follow any structured phases
Because methodology terminology varies between firms and drifts over time, while the underlying work (plan, configure, test, cutover, hypercare) stays consistent
Because only Oracle itself is permitted to name implementation phases
Because naming a methodology would reveal confidential information
questions.explain: Different firms label these phases differently, and naming conventions change over time - but the underlying sequence of work is consistent across methodologies.
